technology.summary: Today's technology news includes a range of topics. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is focusing on how to build an enduring company in the AI era. Apple's "Welcome Home" launch event is expected to include refreshes to Apple TV and HomePod Mini, as well as a new smart home hub and platform. finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have joined forces to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as investors approach October with high crude oil prices, increasing bond yields, and continued foreign selling. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher. Meanwhile, Indian equity benchmarks have experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices.

citations.headline: Sebi, RBI join hands to make onboarding easier for FPIs
Can October turn the tide for Indian stocks after September rout?
El Niño to Compound Drag on Southeast Asian Debt, Analysts Say

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court is set to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a Mumbai protest were detained and threatened with police cases.

In other news, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process "corrupt", citing an Indian election that didn't happen. Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, claiming that his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country. India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by USD 18.34 billion in a single week.

Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
